findings.note: AC-011 (no-flag v1 output byte-identical) cannot be verified from this bundle. Neither bundled test twin contains any byte comparison: the only readable no-flag assertions are structural ('AC-033 matrix no flags: .schema = sdd-run-record/v1', 'has("effort") = false', 'has("capability") = false'), and coder-ac011-mutation-kill.log itself states those pre-existing structural checks do not detect this class of drift. The claimed TEST-011 case, its run_id/generated normalization logic, and the golden fixtures tests/fixtures/emit-run-record/v1-no-flag.{sh,ps1}.golden.json are all absent from the bundle, so the assertion text cannot be read. The only other AC-011 artifact, verification/T-009/baseline.sha256, carries no reproducible '$ <command>' line, includes an unlabelled 'f9de551e...  -' stdin hash, and its pre_/post_ output hashes cannot be recomputed here. Separately, nothing in the bundle shows the new golden fixture was derived from the pre-T-009 emitter (45dda57f^) rather than regenerated from the current one; if it was regenerated, TEST-011 proves self-consistency, not identity with the pre-capability bytes. AC-011 is the sole justification for this task's 'high' risk tier.

Spec drift plus an unasserted error path. Supplying --capability-block-id without --capability-enforcement exits 1 ('--capability-block-id requires --capability-enforcement') before the documented capability-only check runs. design.md's API/Contract Plan states the four reachable flag combinations are 'fixed exhaustively' across exactly two axes, and its rows 1 and 2 (no --capability-enforcement supplied) predict unchanged v1 output and effort-only v2 output; both predictions are violated for this input, since 'feat --capability-block-id X' errors instead of emitting v1 and 'feat --effort-main X --capability-block-id Y' errors instead of emitting effort-only v2. No case in either bundled test twin exercises block-id-alone, so the gate is undocumented and untested on a Security Boundary B2 file under Required Workflow tdd. The implementation report (Specification Differences) and T-009.contract.json both disclose this and explicitly decline to address it; disclosure does not discharge the AC-033 obligation.

findings.ref: reports/implementation/epic-195-a7-compatibility/T-009.md (Outputs table; Test Evidence) vs. T-009.contract.json unit-tests/acceptance-tests evidence
findings.note: The declared-output manifest no longer covers the code that produced the passing evidence. The report declares 'Test Result: PASS (50 passed / 0 failed)' and hashes tests/emit-run-record-feature-scope.tests.ps1 as 318c318498ba3d67a8a0da60f64f30aba91246c5f3db23a9386785d8406b40d6, which I recomputed byte-for-byte from the bundled file (plugins/sdd-quality-loop/scripts/emit-run-record.sh likewise recomputes to the declared 2286b1a8...), confirming the bundle carries the declaration-commit, pre-remediation sources. The contract's two required tdd checks instead pass on coder-acceptance-rerun-2026-08-20.log, a 51/0 run against test files the 2026-08-20 remediation modified, plus new golden fixtures. Those modified files were never re-declared or re-hashed in the Outputs table, so hash-verifying the declared outputs verifies neither the tests that were actually run nor the fixtures they depend on.

Unhandled error path introduced by this task. json_string() shells out to jq -- a dependency used nowhere else in this script and named nowhere in design.md or the task's Planned Files -- and its result is interpolated unchecked into the capability heredoc. The script has no 'set -e' and never inspects jq's exit status, so on a host without jq (or on any jq failure) the command substitution yields the empty string, the emitter writes a malformed record ('  "block_id": ' with no value), and still exits 0 printing 'emit-run-record: wrote ...' -- silent corruption of the cross-epic shared surface the high-risk rationale names. The acceptance suite structurally cannot catch it: its own assert_run_out_eq and jqr helpers invoke jq, so the suite cannot run at all where jq is absent. The PowerShell twin uses in-process ConvertTo-Json and has no equivalent exposure, so the twins diverge in failure mode as well.

An explicitly empty --capability-block-id '' sets capability_block_id_set=1 (PowerShell: ContainsKey is true) and serializes "block_id": "" rather than null. design.md defines block_id only as 'null when --capability-block-id is not supplied' and is silent on supplied-but-empty; no test in either bundled twin covers it. Behaviour is at least consistent across twins, so this is non-blocking, but it is an undefined and unasserted input on a field the design fixes explicitly.

Bundle sanitization over-redacted the PowerShell twin: the regex literals for Status counting, Feature scoping, VERDICT matching and ticket-severity classification are replaced by '[PATH_REDACTED]' (e.g. "$_ -match '^Statu[PATH_REDACTED]'"). Those code paths are unreviewable from the bundle, so any claim about the .ps1 emitter's counting/scoping parity with the .sh twin rests on material I cannot read. T-009's own capability surface and both record-construction branches are intact and readable, so this does not block on its own; recording it because the redaction, not the implementation, is what prevents verification.
